gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the AT-LP70X/LP70XBT's built-in preamp delivers 252 mV line out at 1 kHz, 5 cm/s, versus 140 mV (−17 dBV) for both Fluance RT81 and RT81+. On the same powered speaker, the Audio-Technica plays about 5 dB louder at the same knob position (20·log10(252/140) = 5.1 dB). Fluance publishes the same 140 mV for the RT81+, even though its cartridge is hotter.
standout_why: Compared against valveandvinyl.com/turntables/crosley-alternatives, platterandplinth.com/turntables/best-with-preamp, stylusandsound.com/best-turntables-with-built-in-preamp and fewbetter.com (rank 1; it has no turntable content at all). Valve & Vinyl already normalises the weighting mismatch (AT 'WTD' wow and flutter vs Fluance's unqualified 0.2%; Fluance's A-weighted 67 dB / unweighted 60 dB S/N vs AT's unqualified >55 dB). It also gives AT's 36 dB gain, but it says line output is 'not published' for every deck. Stylus & Sound quotes the RT81+'s 140 mV line output alone and never compares it. Platter & Plinth gives no line-output figure. No page sets 252 mV beside 140 mV or points out that Fluance's line figure doesn't change when the cartridge does.
decides: This confirms rather than overturns ChatGPT's pick, but it sharpens it. For a shopper plugging straight into powered speakers or an AUX input, the AT-LP70X/LP70XBT gives the stronger line signal (about 1.8× the voltage, about 5 dB). The Fluance RT81/RT81+ need more volume-knob travel and will sound quieter than phone or streamer sources on the same input. SECRETS' reviewer named 'higher output (0.5 volts)' as an improvement they wanted on the RT81. The Fluance case rests instead on its true preamp bypass and its published A-weighted S/N. Going from RT81 to RT81+ (+$50) buys the VM95E cartridge, not a louder line out, by Fluance's own spec.

findings.note: Consistency check: 4.0 mV × 10^(36/20) = 4.0 × 63.1 = 252 mV, which matches the stated line level. Same page lists W&F < 0.25% (WTD) and S/N > 55 dB with no weighting stated.

findings.note: Fluance states no test velocity or frequency and no preamp gain (it names only a Texas Instruments preamp IC). Implied gain with the stated 3.5 mV AT95E: 20·log10(140/3.5) = 32.0 dB, about 4 dB below AT's 36 dB, assuming the same reference velocity. Versus the LP70X: 20·log10(252/140) = 5.1 dB quieter.
